The test image shows tomato leaves with numerous small, dark brown to black spots scattered across the leaf surface. The spots appear small (less than 1/4 inch), somewhat circular, with possible halos. The rest of the leaf is green. This is a leaf disease.

Top candidates based on leaf lesion pattern:
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: small circular tan-to-gray lesions with dark perimeter
- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: small angular black spots with yellow halos

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The Septoria reference shows circular spots with dark perimeters and lighter centers - a classic pattern. Comparing to the test image:

- Test image: numerous small dark brown spots scattered across tomato leaves, similar distribution pattern to the Septoria reference
- The spots in the test image are small, numerous, and fairly uniform - consistent with Septoria Leaf Blotch
- No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight), no tan/gray large patches (rules out Late Blight), no obvious white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- The spots appear more uniformly dark brown than the classic tan-center Septoria pattern, but the density and distribution match well
- Bacterial Speck would show tinier pinpoint spots with more obvious yellow halos
